thread:
Anya: rolling back canary now. seeing a 3x p95 on embeddings route and weird cache-miss storms after the new prefetch change. initiating fast cutoff.
Devon: on it. which guard triggered?
Anya: alerts from traffic-guard: latency + kv-miss-rate. console shows a bunch of warm-prefetch requests to older model variant. suspect prefetch TTL overlap.
Samir: oh right we made prefetch kick in on canary to warm KVS. that can cause stray writes to the shared prefix if we didn't namespace correctly.
Jeff: @Samir is this the namespace bug we debated? the one where prefetch used route_id not deployment_id so canary writes could land on prod keys?
Samir: yep. I pushed a tentative fix but not backfilled.
Maya: ops plan? do we do fast revert (scale traffic to 0) or safe-disable (pause prefetch + drain)?
Anya: starting fast cutoff -> set traffic split to 0% for canary and route to fallback model variant. also toggling prefetch off via feature flag.
Li: note: if we cut traffic to 0 without evicting KV prefixes, clients might still get stale responses if they hit cached nodes. recommend issuing KV drain command to region pools: `kvctl drain --prefix canary-2026-03-18 --regions all`
Devon: running kvctl now. will also bump quota-controller to avoid retries from clients spamming on error.
OpsBot: kvctl: drain request accepted for prefixes [canary-2026-03-18]. estimated completion 45s.
Ryan: telemetry: marking this canary with rollback=true in dashboards so the eval graph doesn't treat this as a deploy failure baseline. also flagging the eval-set for embed-quality regressions.
Jeff: small UX ask: can the Console show a single "Abort and Drain" action that does traffic set->0 + kv drain + disable-prefetch? right now it's 3 clicks and easy to miss one.
Samir: internal API debate: do we expose composite actions (atomic rollback) or keep primitives? I argued primitives for safety, but operators want one-click.
Maya: composite action seems useful if we can make it idempotent and auditable. logs must show each substep.
Anya: agree. for this incident I'll go primitives but please prototype composite action. need audit trail for legal.
Devon: kv drain completed in 38s. validating prefixes: `kvctl inspect --prefix canary-2026-03-18` -> empty.
OpsBot: traffic-split update applied: canary=0%, fallback=100%.
Anya: monitoring: p95 trending down. error budget burn stopped.
Ryan: note for postmortem: prefetch writes should always include deployment_id. also consider conservative prefetch for canaries (no shared writes).
Jeff: add a console guard: when enabling prefetch on a canary, require explicit "isolate-kv" checkbox.
Samir: will draft a PR to change prefetch behavior + add namespace enforcement in the runtime.
Maya: also add a canary guard that temporarily sets client retry-window to small so clients don't retry across fallback causing amplification.
Anya: thanks folks. will open rollout-postmortem after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
OpsBot: deploy abort logged by Anya at 1834567901. audit_id: a7f3b2
Anya: filing quick runbook note in #incidents: steps taken, kv drain command, telemetry flags, and console UX request.
Devon: reassigning follow-ups: Samir (prefetch fix), Jeff (console UX), Ryan (telemetry tagging), Maya (retry guard).
Samir: starting PR 4321.
Jeff: mockups incoming.
Maya: adding retry guard to canary guardset.
Anya: closing thread when postmortem is up. thanks everyone.
